case: Criminal complaints naming Mitsotakis over the Tempi rail disaster, forwarded to parliament under Article 86
type: criminal complaints (Mitsotakis named as a suspect by complainants); no prosecution opened
description: On 16 May 2023, days before the 21 May election, relatives of Tempi victims filed a criminal complaint against 17 people 'and anyone responsible', including the boards of the railway operator OSE, Hellenic Train and the Energy Regulatory Authority, past and current transport ministers and Prime Minister Mitsotakis (Ta Nea). On 2 May 2024 a victim's relative, Christos Konstantinidis, filed a further complaint against Mitsotakis and other political figures over the interventions at the crash site, accusing the Prime Minister of usurping executive power and of moral instigation of breach of duty, harbouring an offender and fraud against the State (Alfavita, citing larissanet.gr). In May 2025 the Minister of Justice forwarded to parliament, under Article 86 of the Constitution and the law on ministerial criminal liability, a criminal case file dated 13 May 2025 concerning Mitsotakis, former transport minister Christos Staikouras, former deputy minister Vasileios Oikonomou and deputy minister Nikos Tachiaos, formed after a complaint by 370 citizens including victims' relatives (Parapolitika). Under Article 86 only parliament can decide to investigate or prosecute members of the government. Speaking to ANT1 in May 2023, Mitsotakis described the complaint as 'instrumentalisation' (εργαλειοποίηση) of the tragedy, said he fully understood the relatives' anger and wanted justice at all levels, and added that 'justice is delivered by the courts, not by our political opponents or by third-party judges' (Ta Nea).
outcome: As of October 2026 no proposal to open a parliamentary preliminary investigation into Mitsotakis has been reported in the sources consulted, and he has not been charged. Parliament did open proceedings against former Transport Minister Kostas A. Karamanlis (referred to the Judicial Council in July 2025) and former Deputy Minister Christos Triantopoulos (referred to the Special Court in September 2026), which are listed in the polemics section. The sources do not establish whether the May 2023 complaint and the file of 13 May 2025 are the same case.
court: Prosecuting authorities (complaints); Hellenic Parliament under Article 86 of the Constitution
presumption_note: Mitsotakis was named in complaints filed by private complainants; no prosecutor or parliamentary body has charged him or opened an investigation against him as of October 2026. He has called the 2023 complaint an instrumentalisation of the tragedy and is presumed innocent.
key_facts: 16 May 2023: complaint by victims' relatives against 17 people including the Prime Minister
2 May 2024: supplementary complaint against Mitsotakis over the clearing of the crash site
May 2025: case file dated 13 May 2025, concerning Mitsotakis and three (deputy) ministers, forwarded to parliament under Article 86
No preliminary investigation into Mitsotakis reported as of October 2026
